latest_nl_proof:
Let x \in I_{n,j}. By the intended meaning of the notation in this lemma, I_{n,j} is the half-open cell indexed by j, so x-j/n \in [0,1/n). Define d := x - j/n. Then d is a real number with 0 \le d < 1/n. Also, by the definition of the coordinate map J_{n,j}, we have J_{n,j}(d) = j/n + d = x, so d is a valid witness.

To prove uniqueness, suppose d' \in [0,1/n) also satisfies x = J_{n,j}(d'). Then x = j/n + d', hence d' = x - j/n = d. Therefore no other choice of d is possible.

So there is exactly one real d \in [0,1/n) such that x = J_{n,j}(d), namely d = x - j/n.
role_in_parent: Records uniqueness of the additive coordinate on the half-open cell.
statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. For every real x in I_{n,j}, there is exactly one real d in [0, 1/n) such that x = J_{n,j}(d), namely d = x - j/n.

x is a real number with x in I_{n,j}
d is a real number satisfying 0 <= d < 1/n
the claimed witness satisfies d = x - j/n, so x - j/n must lie in [0, 1/n)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integer n and every integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, for every real x in I_{n,j}, there exists a unique real d such that 0 <= d < 1/n, x equals J_{n,j}(d), and this unique d is exactly x - j/n.
